newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Sharif wins overall majority in Pakistan polls.
newsitem.headline: Sharif wins overall majority in Pakistan polls.

text.p: Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) gained an overall majority in the National Assembly (lower house), according to official results on Tuesday.
With 161 results declared for the 217-seat National Assembly, the PML had won 116 seats for a clear majority. Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) had won only nine.
The PML's position will be bolstered by the performance of its electoral ally, the Awami National Party, which had won eight seats in North West Frontier Province.
Sharif's sweeping victory means he can form a government without having to bargain with possible coalition partners.

The Karachi-based ethnic Mohajir National Movement, which boycotted the last National Assembly election in 1993, won 10 seats, while a PPP splinter faction led by Bhutto's estranged sister-in-law Ghinwa Bhutto gained one seat.
Charismatic cricketer-turned-politician Imran Khan failed to win in any constituency where results had been declared.
